title: Network-Hosted PowerShell Correlated With Destructive Script Content

detection_logic.summary: Correlates network-hosted PowerShell process creation with suspicious execution options and PowerShell operational content containing destructive filesystem operations on the same host within 300 seconds.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: Component A provenance: normalized data.event_id is 1, data.process_image is PowerShell, and data.command_line contains generic UNC syntax with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass and -NoProfile.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: Component B provenance: normalized data.event_id is 4103 and data.script_text contains Remove-Item within PowerShell operational content.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: Baseline process-creation provenance lacks PowerShell image, generic UNC syntax, and suspicious PowerShell execution options in normalized data fields.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: A high-confidence result is expected when Component A and Component B occur on the same normalized host within 300 seconds; isolated component matches are expected to be medium confidence.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: No correlated matches are expected when baseline records do not contain both the network-hosted suspicious PowerShell execution pattern and destructive PowerShell content.

limitations: PowerShell Event IDs 4103 and 4104 depend on logging configuration and may be absent.
Correlation uses normalized host and a five-minute window; without cross-source process identifiers, unrelated activity on the same host can be joined.
Generic UNC PowerShell execution and destructive filesystem commands can be legitimate administrative or maintenance activity.
A Component A-only or Component B-only result is medium confidence and requires analyst review.

deployment_target.description: Windows machine running the Project Janus Python scripts
deployment_target.destination: Project Janus controller proposed active-rules location
